_comment: index.json - the FIRST-PARTY SET. Record §6.3: 'a shipped index, not canon'.
DATA. NO IMPORTS. DIFFABLE. RELEASED WITH THE WHEEL. It is the authority for exactly one
question: which mac.-prefixed connector ids are real, and where is the JSON Schema that
WHY THIS IS NOT A MEMBER LIST IN mac_vocabulary.yaml. The first draft put `athena` and `duckdb`
into the canon as vocabulary members, which is the exact act §3's boundary table forbids - 'no
vendor product name in mac_vocabulary.yaml or mac.schema.json'. The canon registers the
NAMESPACE and nothing else. This file is software: versioned with the distribution and
diffable across releases by an ordinary snapshot test, which is the property the member list
was supposed to provide and did not.
AND IT IS WHAT LETS A MOUNT VALIDATE A CONFIG WITH ZERO IMPORTS. The dry half of the contract
is @classmethod - pure functions of the config mapping - so for a first-party connector,
mount-time validation is jsonschema.validate(config, <a file in this repo>). No import, no
loader, no deadline, no ambiguity, no squatting corroboration.
RULING 14 IS UNANSWERED, so there is no third-party half of this file and no discovery
mechanism beside it. §11.2: if the answer is 'no third party now', the registry collapses to
exactly a dict of first-party classes resolved from this index - which is what registry.py is.
The `target` field is read by that module; it is a module:attr pair, never a path.
